title: Data Structures Review: Build Anything
story: You've built playlists, contacts, shopping carts, colors, timers, dice rollers, seasons, difficulty levels, coffee orders, card games, safe math chains, config parsers, search functions, temperature alerts, validators, week planners, robot commands, and treasure chests. Now synthesize everything into a single showcase.
why: Review and synthesis: combine structs, enums, methods, nesting, and matching across multiple domains in one file.
analogy: You're now a data architect. Structs are your bricks. Enums are your paint colors. Methods are your blueprints. Match is your construction crew that reads the blueprint and decides which wall to build next. Every building in town uses the same materials — the difference is how you arrange them.
try_it: Combine two of your types into a new struct. For example: combine Movie and Genre into a `CatalogEntry` struct. Combine Order and a `Customer` struct. Combine Chord and Note into a `Song` struct that holds a sequence of chords. There are no wrong answers.
tips: Start with the nouns (structs), then the choices (enums), then the verbs (methods)
Every domain breaks down the same way: what data exists? what choices? what actions?
If two structs share fields, consider nesting one inside the other
Build incrementally: define one struct, test it, add an enum, test again
common_mistakes: Trying to fit everything into one giant struct — split into smaller, focused types
Making every field an enum when a simple type would do — enums are for CHOICES, not values
Defining types in the wrong order — types used by other types must be defined first
